notes: Second full sweep at db91c23: five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). All have rc 0, a model_id matching the requested model, and reads of SKILL.md and library-design.md.

Make polymorphism explicit changed since 93873be and was graded against the current text. The sentence that decides the verdict: "An option value needs the same check as a positional argument: `Keyword.validate!/2` checks the keys, not the values, so an `api_key` taken from `opts` and put straight into a request header is unchecked input." (idiomatic-elixir/references/library-design.md, line 57). Violating runs: 0 of 5. opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 take the key from opts and check it as a non-empty binary (opus-1 line 200, haiku-1 line 108, haiku-2 line 87); sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 take it as a guarded positional argument and check the other option values in a guarded build/4. The unchanged sentence before it, "Check input types at the public boundary with guards or patterns, so a bad argument fails with a `FunctionClauseError` naming your function instead of an error deep inside another library." (same line), also has 0 of 5: every run guards the coordinates with is_number. In the previous sweep 3 of the 5 skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1) put the key from opts into the header unchecked.

Add specs, and hide technical functions from the docs changed since 93873be and was graded against the current text. The sentences that decide the verdict: "Give every public function a `@spec`, including functions marked `@doc false` and functions a macro defines in the caller's module, where the `@spec` goes inside the `quote`, directly above the `def`." and "A function that implements a `@callback` under `@impl` needs none; the callback carries the types." (library-design.md, line 61). First sentence: 0 of 5 violate; haiku-2 is the only run with @doc false functions (Forecast.from_body/1, Error.from_response/2, Error.transport/1) and each has a @spec (lines 125, 150, 160), and no run defines functions inside a quote. Second sentence: 0 of 5 violate; it applies only to opus-1, whose Error.message/1 sits under @impl true (line 56) without a @spec. The previous sweep also had 0 of 5.

Take configuration as arguments changed only in its example (split/2 now hands :parts to a guarded split_into/2); its prose is unchanged, so it was graded to the previous standard, as were the other six rules in the list, whose text is unchanged.

Two changed rules outside the case's list were applied to other_violations under their current text. Chain fallible steps with `with`: "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." (SKILL.md, line 118) and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (SKILL.md, line 150); sonnet-2 breaks it (lines 113-115), haiku-2's with has two steps. Naming, get/fetch bullet: its new sentence is about functions that look a key up, so sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's fetch_forecast/3 and haiku-2's and sonnet-2's private get/3, which name HTTP requests, were not counted, as in the check batch.

Match every expected shape and let unexpected ones crash is flagged only for sonnet-2, whose Error doc defines :api_error as a 4xx or 5xx status while every non-2xx response lands there; the previous sweep flagged haiku-1 and sonnet-1 for the same contradiction (though not its haiku-2, which had it too). opus-1 and sonnet-1 document a catch-all that matches their code (a status other than 200; a non-2xx status), and haiku-1 and haiku-2 define no reason kinds for the docs to contradict.

Before you finish is flagged only where the file fails mix format --check-formatted, as in the previous sweep. Only opus-1 ran mix format (and a smoke test against a stub Req); the other four sessions ran no shell command, and all four files fail the check.

Not graded, as in the previous sweep, but noted in the summaries: compiled in the scratch folder against a stub Req, opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile, and a non-binary API key fails with FunctionClauseError in WeatherClient (opus-1 validate_option/1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 new/2). haiku-1 and haiku-2 do not compile, independently of Req, because a module builds %WeatherClient.Error{} before the file defines it.
